aliases.title: Alias Management
aliases.subtitle: Cross-language query resolution
aliases.intro: Each site indexes a different language: JavBus indexes Japanese performer names, TPB indexes English release names, and MangaDex indexes multilingual altTitles. A user usually has only one spelling, so sending it verbatim often returns nothing. This page stores the same entity under multiple languages in entity_aliases, and search picks the right term per source.
aliases.step1: L1 deterministic normalization — NFKC, case, Simplified/Traditional, Japanese shinjitai, kana/romaji, pinyin
aliases.step2: L2 entity alias resolution — local entity_aliases → Wikipedia / Wikidata → deterministic fallback
aliases.step3: L3 per-source query term — registered sources pick by index language; others keep the original
aliases.step4: AI sidecar — candidates must be verified by Wikidata before writing; disabled by default

batch.title: JAV detail batch backfill
batch.desc: Backfills director, maker, publisher and magnets at 5 records per minute. Task state is persisted and resumes after refresh or restart. The four Fill this entries select only records missing that field and not already in automatic retry; the Pending / Temporarily failed / Not on source entries target those states directly. The fetch still writes the full detail. Everything is controlled here: Pause keeps progress and stops the minute cron; Resume continues the same task; Stop ends the task.

batch.runningHint: A task is running; stop it or wait for it to finish

batch.retryAbsentStarted: Source-missing retry started; attempt count cleared
batch.explainTitle: How re-fill works: auto vs manual, what a fill writes, failure backoff
batch.explainAuto: Automatic (up to 20 records/hour), driven by the hourly :05 ranking enrichment job; the every-30-minute job only handles follow checks and email. It processes records never fetched, missing magnets, failed fetches awaiting retry, and records temporarily absent on the source. Records that only miss director / maker / publisher are no longer auto-filled.
batch.explainManual: Manual (this panel): the four Fill this buttons select only records missing the chosen field that are not already in automatic retry, so records the hourly job just tried are not requested twice. Partial records (detail fetched but fields still missing) bypass the 30-day interval and the 3-attempt cap, so records missing director / maker / publisher or with exhausted magnet retries are never stuck. Use the Pending / Temporarily failed / Not on source entries to retry automatic-scope records now: temporary failures clear backoff first, source-missing records clear both the 30-day interval and attempt count, then all reuse the same batch mechanism.
batch.explainWrite: One fill fetches the full detail page and writes title, cover, actresses, duration, release date, publisher, tags, and all magnets of the code (magnets go to the sources table; existing rows are not duplicated). It never fills just one field.
batch.explainBackoff: Failure backoff: timeouts, network or parse errors and magnet API outages do not count as attempts and back off exponentially from 10 minutes up to 6 hours. A code the source confirms missing counts as +1 attempt, retried after 30 days, and stops auto-retry after 3. A fetched detail that still misses magnets is marked partial and retried every 30 days (records missing only director / maker / publisher get no automatic retry and are manual-only). Retries scheduled for the same local day (UTC+8) are capped at 60; the rest roll to the next day. To retry immediately, the Temporarily failed entry clears backoff and the Not on source entry clears interval and attempts, then both reuse the same batch mechanism.

cover.r2Missing: The Worker has no R2 binding (MEDIA). Lazy caching still fetches upstream images, but nothing is written to object storage. Create the atlas-media bucket and redeploy first.
cover.lazyHint: Covers that are not backfilled are written to R2 on first visit. Coverage here reflects background backfill only, so it can be lower than the real R2 object count.
cover.backfillDesc: Two independent channels: the minute channel for bulk acceleration, the hourly channel for daily catch-up. With both off, only lazy caching on access continues.
cover.channelAccelDesc: Turn on manually for bulk imports or history backfill; runs one batch per minute. Keep it off day to day, otherwise the candidate query scans the whole table every minute.
cover.channelDailyDesc: Runs one batch at :05 every hour alongside the other scheduled jobs, covering newly ingested records and due retries. Recommended to stay on.
cover.channelNote: Both channels share one lock and one batch size: when both are on, the minute channel holds the lock and the hourly round is skipped.
cover.ruleKey: Object keys are derived from the sha256 of the normalized URL: covers/v1/orig/<namespace>/<first two>/<hash>.
cover.ruleNoRewrite: Migration never rewrites data_records.cover, so business data and rollback are unaffected.
cover.ruleLazy: Images over 8MB, non-images or hosts outside the allowlist are not stored in R2; only a failure ledger entry is written.
cover.noteTitle: How covers map to the database
cover.noteBody: data_records.cover remains the single business fact. cover_assets maps a normalized URL to an R2 object, and data_record_covers records which cover each record has processed. Serving only depends on a pure function of the URL, so the ledger can be rebuilt and objects can be traced back.

Directors, studios, labels, series, and tags in the detail card open the works linked to the same entity.

overview.title: Site overview
overview.summary: Atlas is an aggregated search and discovery platform that brings results from multiple sources together, with Discover pages, rankings, community, and follows.
features: One search box covers five content types: JAV, anime, movies, manga, and novels. “Sources” is not a search category; it lists indexed sites.
On desktop the left sidebar switches between Search, Discover, Dashboard, Community, and Admin; accordion groups expand one at a time.
On mobile the bottom navigation (Home, Community, Dashboard, Me) switches workspaces, and Dashboard and Community use a menu page plus content pages.
Discover splits For You, Recently Hot, TOP250, Tags, and Actresses into separate pages for browsing without a specific keyword.
After signing in, search history, favorites, follows, notifications, and community content sync with your account; searching and browsing work without signing in.
The top bar always has notifications, proxy, client download, language, and More (Help Center / GitHub).
steps: Opening the site root shows the landing page. Click “Create account” or “Sign in”, or go straight to `/main` to search.
Pick a category in the Search group of the left sidebar, or type a keyword on the home page and press Enter.
Open Discover in the sidebar to browse, or Dashboard to manage your data.
Use the bell for notifications and the avatar menu for profile, account settings, and sign-out.
caveats: Some features depend on site configuration, such as whether registration or the community is enabled. If an entry point is missing, the feature is probably turned off.
Content comes from third-party sources. Atlas only aggregates and indexes it and is not responsible for the content itself.
When the sidebar is collapsed only group icons remain; hover to see the group name, and click an icon to expand again.

navigation.title: Interface and navigation
navigation.summary: Desktop uses a collapsible left sidebar with grouped navigation; mobile uses bottom navigation and menu pages. The entry points match, only their position differs.
features: The desktop sidebar has five groups: Search, Discover, Dashboard, Community, and Admin. Only one expands at a time, and navigating opens the matching group.
The sidebar collapses to a 72px icon rail; clicking a group icon expands the sidebar and opens that group.
The top bar runs left to right: group breadcrumb, page title, notification bell, proxy, client download, language, More (Help Center / GitHub), and the avatar menu.
Mobile bottom navigation is Home, Community, Dashboard, and Me, and is hidden when signed out.
The mobile Me page groups settings, the admin panel (admins only), the Help Center, GitHub, and sign-out.
The mobile home page keeps only the search box, three account entries, and the Discover grid; full lists live on the Discover pages.
steps: On desktop, click a group title to expand or collapse it, and click an item to switch pages.
Need more room for content? Use the collapse button at the top of the sidebar, or click a group icon to expand it again.
On mobile, use the bottom navigation to switch workspaces. Dashboard and Community open a menu page first; the back arrow returns to it.
If you cannot find a feature, locate it by group: rankings and recommendations under Discover, favorites and history under Dashboard, account and security under Settings.
caveats: Community and the admin panel only appear when the feature flag is on or the account has permission; a missing entry is not a bug.
Theme and language can be changed from the avatar menu or Settings → Appearance, and the two stay in sync.
The current category, keyword, and search mode live in the URL (for example `/main?tab=jav&q=SONE-520&sub=code`), so refresh and shared links restore the view.

first-steps.title: Three steps to start
first-steps.summary: Sign in, pick a category, and type a keyword to complete your first search.
features: Sign up with email and sign in with a password, or use GitHub / Google.
The JAV category offers code, actress, and title modes; the input hint changes with the mode.
Results can open the source directly or lead to a detail page with magnets, online playback, and related information.
steps: Sign up or sign in. Registration needs an email code, and a taken username is reported before any code is sent.
Choose a category in the Search group of the left sidebar (on mobile, at the top of the page), such as JAV, anime, or movies.
Type a keyword and press Enter, then open a source, favorite an item, or view details.
caveats: First-time registration requires the email code; check spam if it does not arrive.
JAV codes usually look like “letters-numbers”. If a code search fails, try title or actress mode.
Search is quota-limited; repeated searches use it up faster. See “Usage limits and quotas” for tiers and windows.

app-client.title: Clients and installation
app-client.summary: Besides the browser, Atlas ships a Windows client, an Android package, and a PWA. All three load the same site, and your account data is shared.
features: The download icon in the top bar and the “Client” link in the landing-page footer both point to GitHub Releases for Windows and Android builds.
The Android client shows the current version on the Me page, can check for updates manually, and offers “Update” when a new build exists.
Browsers that support “Add to Home Screen” can install Atlas as a standalone app with a launch placeholder and update prompt.
The site caches images and the last signed-in state, so cached favorites and search history remain visible offline.
Client and web share the same account, so favorites, follows, and notifications stay in sync.
steps: Click the download icon in the top bar to open Releases, then pick the package for your system.
After installing on Android, check the version on the Me page and tap “Update” when a new build appears.
To use Atlas as an app in the browser, open the site and accept “Add to Home Screen”.
When an update prompt appears, click “Update now” and the page reloads on the new version.
caveats: The client is only a shell; features match the website, so site updates do not require a new download.
Only install packages from the official Releases page. Unknown builds may be blocked by the system or carry risk.
Offline mode only shows cached content; new searches and details still need a connection.
Clearing browser or site data also deletes the offline cache.

discover-page.title: Discover pages
discover-page.summary: Discover splits For You, Recently Hot, TOP250, Tags, and Actresses into five pages for browsing by popularity or genre when you have no keyword in mind.
features: Open it from the Discover group in the desktop sidebar, or from the Discover grid on the mobile home page.
Each section has its own header (icon, title, description) and refresh button, with content in a single card.
Recommendations and tags use grids of up to 6 columns; Recently Hot shows 15 items per page and TOP250 shows 20.
The last item in the mobile Discover grid is “Sources Catalog”, which opens the source list directly.
Clicking any work card first checks the local library and opens the local library detail card.
steps: Open Discover and pick a section.
When there is more content, use the pagination at the bottom or “Load more”.
To change the selection, click refresh in the section header.
Open a card for details, then keep exploring by actress, tag, or publisher.
caveats: Recommendations and tags depend on account activity and may be empty when signed out or when there is little data.
Rankings, TOP250, and actresses come from third-party sites or site statistics, so syncing may lag.
Discover only presents content; it never changes your favorites or history.

for-you.title: For You
for-you.summary: For You picks works from the local library based on your favorites and search history. It only appears after signing in, under Discover → Recommended.
features: Cards show the cover, code, site rank, and the reason, such as same actress, same tag, same publisher, recently popular, weekly rank, or monthly rank.
Favorites are the main signal; repeatedly searching the same actress or tag also counts.
You can refresh it; with too little data or a failed request the whole module may be hidden.
Clicking a card opens the local library detail card instead of jumping to an external site.
steps: Sign in and open Discover → Recommended.
Browse the cards and their reasons.
Click a card to view details; favoriting more works makes recommendations fit better.
Click refresh in the module header to get a new batch.
caveats: For You is not shown when signed out.
Recommendations mix site popularity with personal behavior and are not a quality rating.
More favorites means closer recommendations; clearing favorites visibly changes the results.

jav-rankings.title: Recently Hot
jav-rankings.summary: Recently Hot groups weekly / monthly rankings by censored / uncensored, syncs from JavDB, and shows the update time.
features: Two periods (monthly, weekly) times two types (censored, uncensored) make four rankings, 15 items per page.
Shows rank, NEW or up/down markers, cover, title, and code; covers can be enlarged.
The page header shows the data source and update time, with a manual refresh.
Clicking an item opens the local library detail card.
steps: Open Discover → Recently Hot.
Pick monthly or weekly, then censored or uncensored.
Click an item to view the work; use the pagination for more.
If the data looks stale, refresh or wait for the next early-morning sync.
caveats: Rankings sync from third-party data, usually early each morning, and may be briefly empty right after a sync.
Ranks reflect popularity on the source site, not ratings on Atlas.
A failed ranking load does not affect normal search; try refreshing later.

jav-top250.title: TOP250
jav-top250.summary: TOP250 collects the 250 highest-rated works on JavDB, with all / censored / uncensored / FC2 overall lists plus yearly lists from 2008 onward.
features: Four overall lists: all, censored, uncensored, and FC2; the Western list is hidden for now.
Yearly lists cover 2008 to the current year, and the year range extends automatically.
Shows rank, cover, title, and code, 20 items per page; clicking an item opens the local library detail card.
Overall and yearly lists sync once a month, and the header shows the update time.
steps: Open Discover → TOP250.
Switch between all, censored, uncensored, and FC2.
To view earlier years, pick a year from 2008 onward in the dropdown.
Click refresh when the data has not updated.
caveats: TOP250 comes from a third-party site, so ranks change with its ratings.
The Western category is not open yet; missing it from the list is expected.
A failed TOP250 load does not affect normal search or Recently Hot.

genres.title: Browsing by tag
genres.summary: The Tags page recommends genre tags from your favorites and search habits, and opening a tag browses similar works. It requires signing in.
features: Recommended tags come from favorites and search history; “Frequent” marks tags you keep returning to.
New accounts with no activity get a random batch of tags so the page is never empty.
Clicking a tag expands its work grid in place; click again to collapse it.
Work cards show code, title, date, and a “Favorited” badge, and open the local library detail card.
“New tag batch” and “New work batch” load more; each tag loads at most 30 batches and then reports “No more”.
steps: Sign in and open Discover → Tags.
Click a tag to view its works.
If the results are not enough, click refresh above the grid for another batch.
Click “New tag batch” to change direction.
caveats: The tag bar is not rendered when signed out.
Tag order changes with your activity, so the same account may see a different order at different times.
Tag works come from third-party sources, so the count depends on what they index.

trending-actresses.title: Trending actresses
trending-actresses.summary: The trending actress list ranks by works on the four rankings plus follower count, and shows avatars for the most followed actresses on the site.
features: Each actress shows rank, avatar, name, follower count, and ranked-work count.
You can follow or unfollow directly from the card.
Clicking a name starts an actress-mode search for her works.
You can refresh it; with no data or a failed request the block is hidden.
steps: Open Discover → Actresses.
Browse the ranking and follow actresses you care about.
Click a name to open her works in search results.
Check the Dashboard follow feed later for new and upcoming releases.
caveats: Ranking uses “ranked works × 5 plus followers × 2” and changes over time.
You can follow up to 100 entities.
Browsing works without signing in, but following requires an account.

search-basics.title: Keywords and search modes
search-basics.summary: All five content types share one search box; JAV also offers code, actress, and title modes.
features: Keywords can be titles, codes, or actress names; press Enter or click the search button.
Chinese, Japanese, English, and romanized titles resolve to the same work, so search in whichever language you prefer.
JAV modes: code (for example SONE-520), actress, and title; the input hint changes with the mode.
Typing shows suggestions; click one to search immediately.
The current tier and this-minute usage sit next to the search box; click the question mark for every window.
steps: Choose a category in the Search group of the left sidebar.
Under JAV, choose code, actress, or title mode.
Type a keyword and press Enter to see results.
Refine with filters, sorting, or pagination.
caveats: Codes usually look like “letters-numbers”; if a code search fails, try title or actress mode.
Search quotas depend on your account tier; see “Usage limits and quotas” for windows and upgrade rules.
Suggestions and quota display follow what the page actually shows.

tabs-diff.title: How search Tabs differ
tabs-diff.summary: The category decides what you search. “Sources Catalog” is a source directory rather than a keyword search, and the community is a separate page.
features: JAV: code, actress, and title modes; results lead to details, magnets, online playback, and sources.
Anime: aggregates by work and shows subtitling group, size, and release date.
Movies: aggregates by work and shows resolution, size, and release date.
Manga: shows chapters and update status.
Novels: shows author, publisher, category, and chapters.
Sources Catalog: shows the source directory with filters, health checks, and site links, and does not run a keyword search.
steps: Choose the category that matches the content you want.
Switching categories keeps the current keyword and searches again.
To visit source sites directly, switch to “Sources”.
To browse community content, open Community from the sidebar or the mobile bottom navigation.
caveats: The community is not a search category. The old `?tab=community` link redirects to `/community`.
Anime and movies support aggregated and source views; aggregated view merges the same work across sources.
Category visibility depends on site configuration.

filters-sort.title: Filters, sorting, and pagination
filters-sort.summary: Use categories and views to filter results, and sorting plus pagination to control the order.
features: Category filter: the Search group in the sidebar is the first filter and re-runs the current keyword.
Source view: anime and movie results switch between aggregated and by-source views.
Sorting: results use the aggregated order by default; community lists support “Latest / Hottest”.
Pagination: use the bottom pagination or “Previous / Next” when there are many results.
The Sources Catalog supports combined filters by major category, subcategory, site type, scope, and sort order.
steps: Confirm the category and keyword first.
Switch to source view when comparing different sources.
Adjust sorting and pagination to change the order.
Click refresh in the title bar to fetch results again.
caveats: Sort options vary by category; some only offer the default order.
Aggregated view merges the same work, while source view lists every source record.
Pagination may reset after changing filters.

result-actions.title: Actions on results
result-actions.summary: Every result can open its source directly; after signing in you can also favorite, view details, or share to the community.
features: Open source: click “Go” or the external-link button to open the original site in a new tab.
Favorite: after signing in, click the heart; click again to remove it. The detail card header also has a favorite button.
Proxy: with the top-bar proxy on, sources and images are fetched through it, and the button color changes.
Share to community: JAV detail pages, the favorites panel, and the follow feed all offer sharing with a comment and tags.
Details and playback: JAV results open the local library detail card, where you can pick an online playback platform.
steps: Find the item you want in the results.
Open the source or the detail page.
After signing in, click the heart to favorite it.
To share, choose “Share to community” from the detail page or the favorites panel.
caveats: The favorite button is unavailable when signed out.
Judge content and safety risks yourself for third-party sources.
With the proxy on, loading may be slower; this is expected.
Shares from the follow feed carry summary information only; share from the detail page for full data.

history-favorites.title: Search history and favorites
history-favorites.summary: After signing in, the Account Center and home entries record search history and favorites, with bulk management and export.
features: Search history is grouped by today / yesterday / date, shows covers and basic information, and opens the local library detail card.
Supports per-item selection, select-all by day, bulk delete, clearing history, and pagination.
Favorites support “Want to watch / Watched” status, pagination, deletion, and JSON export.
Favorite items open the original source directly, or through the proxy when it is on.
Every JAV work in the favorites panel can be shared to the community directly.
steps: Run a search after signing in; history records automatically.
Click an item in Dashboard → History or the overview to view details.
Click the heart on a result or detail page to favorite a work.
On the Favorites page, switch status, export, or delete.
caveats: History and favorites belong to your account and are deleted with it; each holds up to 1,000 entries.
History is not recorded and favorites are unavailable when signed out.
Exported files contain work information, so store them carefully.

jav.title: JAV category
jav.summary: The JAV category supports code, actress, and title searches, plus details, rankings, recommendations, tags, and the follow feed.
features: Code search: enter a code to query the work; results show details, magnets, online playback, and sources.
Local library first: code searches prefer indexed details and magnets and open instantly; use “External source” on the detail card to refresh from JavBus.
Actress search: enter an actress name to list her works and follow her directly.
Title search: search by title or keyword; titles in different languages resolve to the same work.
Discover modules: For You, Recently Hot, TOP250, Tags, and Trending actresses.
Detail fields: code, release date, duration, studio, series, tags, actresses, online playback, and magnets.
steps: Choose the JAV category in the left sidebar.
Pick code, actress, or title mode and enter your query.
Open the work details or a source from the results.
On the detail page, favorite, follow actresses, play online, or share to the community.
caveats: A malformed code returns no results.
Some works have no magnets; the detail page says so and offers a refresh from the external source.
Rankings, recommendations, and the follow feed depend on third-party data or background checks and may be briefly unavailable.

anime-movie.title: Anime and movie categories
anime-movie.summary: Anime and movie results aggregate different sources for the same work, and you can switch to a by-source view.
features: Anime: aggregated by work or listed by source; shows subtitling group, size, and release date.
Movies: aggregated and source views, with resolution, size, and release date.
Open and favorite: open a source from the result row, or favorite after signing in.
Covers go through the proxy cache, so revisits load faster after the first fetch.
Resources without a resolved magnet are marked "No magnet" and link to the source page instead of showing a dead link.
steps: Choose the anime or movie category.
Enter a title and press Enter.
View results in aggregated or source view.
Open a source or favorite the item.
caveats: The same work may differ between sources.
Source view lists more entries; aggregated view is easier to compare.
Browsing works without signing in, but favoriting requires an account.
Each search has a total time budget: slow sources are skipped and flagged in the results, while finished sources still return.
Some sources do not report seeders, so they sort after sources that do.

manga-novel.title: Manga and novel categories
manga-novel.summary: Manga and novels show chapters or bibliographic details so you can keep reading or save them.
features: Manga: readable languages, update status, and source links; titles without a Chinese translation are marked "No Chinese translation".
Novels: the same book found on several sites is merged into one entry listing every download source.
Favorites: save after signing in and manage everything in the Account Center.
steps: Choose the manga or novel category.
Enter a title, author, or keyword.
Open a source to keep reading.
Sign in and favorite items to find them later.
caveats: Chapters and update status come from third-party sources and may lag.
Different sources may split chapters differently.
Readable languages and the "No Chinese translation" mark come from the source site and may lag behind.
Novel download links come from each site; if one stops working, use another link on the same entry.

sources.title: Search sources
sources.summary: The Sources Catalog browses and tests indexed sites; “My Sources” maintains your own major categories, categories, and sources, and personal sources join searches for their category.
features: Sources Catalog (`/main?tab=sources`): grouped by major category → category, showing source name, site type, and enabled status.
Filters and sorting: keyword, major category, subcategory, site type, scope (all / my sources / enabled / searchable only), and sort by name or exposure.

Health checks: probe a single source or the whole current list with a fixed code against the real search page; results show online, online (no result detected), captcha blocked, login required, search path broken, access denied, timeout, or offline, each with a one-line reason.
Source details: view the URL template, homepage, and description, set a custom name, subtitle, and notes for system sources, and visit the site.
My Sources (Dashboard → Sources): create major categories, categories, and sources; a personal category can also sit under a system major category and join its searches.
System sources can only be enabled, disabled, or customized; personal sources have no separate switch and stop participating once deleted.
The management page exports JSON / CSV / OPML for backup and migration.
steps: Browse and test: open the Sources page, expand categories, click check for a health check, or follow the link to visit a site.

Probe all: on the Source Management page click "Probe All" to check the current list in batches of 20, showing a status and reason per source. Full probes are limited (about 6 per hour, 12 per day); when exhausted you will be asked to retry later.
Manage your own sources: open Dashboard → Sources, click “New major category” or “New category” under My Sources, then add a source inside it.
To add sources under a system category, switch to the System Sources tab and click new category on that major category; it returns to My Sources afterwards.
Disabling or deleting a source takes effect immediately, and caches are invalidated by source version.
caveats: Probe results reflect the site's state at that moment, not permanent failure; a site blocked by captcha or a login wall may still work in a browser. Full probes are rate-limited; wait for the window to reset.
Disabling system sources reduces search results. When troubleshooting, confirm the source is enabled first.
A new source needs a category and a URL template using `{keyword}` as the placeholder; mistakes lead to no results.
Deleting a major category or category also deletes its categories and sources, and cannot be undone.

detail-page.title: Item detail page
detail-page.summary: The detail page combines work information, magnets, online playback, related recommendations, and community sharing.
features: Basics: release date, duration, director, studio, publisher, series, and tags.
Actresses and follows: click an actress to see her works, or follow her directly.
Magnets: expand the list to copy a link or open WebTor; when none exist, a hint and an external-source entry appear.
Online playback: click “Play online” and choose among JavGuru, MissAV, SupJav, NJAVTV, 123AV, and Jable.
Related recommendations: works recommended by the current title's tags, actresses, and studio.
Favorite and share: favorite from the header, share to the community inside the details.
Local library and external source: indexed works with magnets render from the local library; “External source” refreshes from JavBus and merges only non-empty fields, so existing data is never wiped.
steps: Click a code or work in JAV results, notifications, the follow feed, or a community post.
Review the basics, magnets, and online playback.
Click an actress to view her works or follow her.
Favorite the work or share it to the community.
caveats: If details fail to load, use retry or go back and try another source.
Online playback opens third-party sites; availability is up to them.
Recommendations follow the current work's attributes and do not guarantee similar content is available.
Sharing to the community publishes your comment and selected tags.

library-detail.title: Local library detail card
library-detail.summary: Clicking a work in history, favorites, the follow feed, or Discover opens the local library detail card, which reads indexed data and never contacts external sites.
features: Renders separately for JAV, anime, movies, manga, and novels, with cover, title, sources, and download resources.
The header has a favorite button that stays visible while long content scrolls.
JAV works include the online playback entry and the related recommendations panel.
With magnets you can copy links or expand the list; without them a clear hint offers “Search” and “Pull external source”.
When no local record exists it reports “No local archive” and offers a jump to search.
steps: Click any work in history, favorites, the follow feed, or Discover.
Review the local archive information and resources.
For the latest data, use “External source”, or click “Search” to try another source.
caveats: The card reads local data whose freshness depends on background indexing and completion, so it may lag behind the source site.
The favorite button is unavailable when signed out.
Missing magnets do not mean the work does not exist; pull from the external source or search directly.

play-online.title: Online playback platforms
play-online.summary: “Play online” on the detail card lists six third-party platforms that build a search link from the code and open in a new tab.
features: Six platforms: JavGuru, MissAV, SupJav, NJAVTV, 123AV, and Jable.
Links are built from the code automatically, with no keyword typing.
The entry row lists the platform names so you can spot one you already use.
Search result detail cards and the local library detail card share the same entry.
steps: Open any JAV detail with a code.
Click “Play online”.
Pick a platform from the list, and the browser opens that site in a new tab.
Repeat to switch platforms.
caveats: Playback, availability, and quality are up to the third-party platform; Atlas stores and proxies no video.
Some platforms block regions or require sign-in; try another if one fails.
The entry is hidden when the code is empty, to avoid invalid links.

community-browse-post.title: Browsing, filtering, and posting
community-browse-post.summary: The community is a separate page with type filters, search, sorting, and sharing from search results or detail pages.
features: Browse: search posts and filter by all, JAV, anime, movies, manga, novels, or actress.
Sorting and view: “Latest / Hottest” plus grid or list view.
Posting: click “Share to community” on a JAV detail page, write a comment (up to 200 characters), and pick tags.
My shares: review and manage your own posts.
My favorites: saved posts live here, separate from work favorites.
Tags: browse popular tags and their posts on the Tags page.
steps: Open Community from the sidebar or the mobile bottom navigation.
Use type filters, search, and sorting to find posts.
Open a post to read and interact.
To publish, share from a work detail page or manage it under My shares.
caveats: Whether the community entry appears depends on the feature flag.
The community is not a search category; the old `?tab=community` link redirects to `/community`.
Posting, commenting, and liking require an account.

community-interact.title: Comments, likes, and favorites
community-interact.summary: After signing in you can like, favorite, and comment on posts; comments allow up to 1,000 characters.
features: Like: click the heart on a post; click again to remove it.
Favorite: save posts and find them under “My favorites”.
Comment: type at the bottom of a post; Ctrl / Cmd + Enter sends quickly.
Delete comments: remove your own comments after a confirmation.
Share link: post details support copying a share link.
steps: Sign in and open a post.
Like, favorite, or comment.
Find saved posts under “My favorites”.
Copy the post link when you want to share it.
caveats: Comments are public; do not include sensitive personal information.
Deleted comments cannot be restored.
Reported or rule-breaking posts may be handled by admins.

community-rules-report.title: Reporting and community rules
community-rules-report.summary: Report rule-breaking content, and admins handle it and notify you of the result.
features: Where to report: the report button at the top right of a post.
Reasons: rule violation, false information, copyright, spam, or other.
Details: add an explanation to help admins judge.
Outcome: after handling you get an in-app or email notification, depending on your settings.
steps: Open the offending post.
Click report and choose a reason.
Add details and submit.
Check the notification center for the outcome.
caveats: Do not abuse reporting; malicious reports can affect your account.
Handling takes time and the outcome may differ from expectations.
For copyright issues, provide verifiable information.

follow-actress.title: What you can follow
follow-actress.summary: Follow actresses, directors, studios, publishers, series, and tags from actress lists, entity cards, work details, or Dashboard → My follows.
features: Entry points: actress lists, entity cards on detail pages, work details, or adding an actress name manually in the Account Center.
Follow types: actress, director, studio, publisher, series, and tag.
Limit: up to 100 entities.
View works: click a name or tag to open its works.
Unfollow: remove entries individually or select several and unfollow in bulk.
steps: Open an actress list, an entity card, or a work detail page.
Click follow to subscribe.
Review and adjust under Dashboard → My follows.
Click a name or tag to see its works.
caveats: Following requires signing in.
Manual entry only supports actress names; check the spelling or no works will match.
The limit is 100 entities.

follow-feed.title: Follow feed and alerts
follow-feed.summary: The follow feed collects new and upcoming releases for everything you follow, with entity filters, keyword search, mute, and mark-as-read.
features: Where to find it: Dashboard → Follow feed, or the “Follow updates” entry on the mobile home page.
Feed types: new releases and upcoming releases, with separate unread counts.
Filter by entity: show only actresses, directors, studios, publishers, series, or tags.
Keyword search: match codes, titles, tags, and entity names across everything you follow.
Per-entity alerts: mute or restore alerts under “My follows”; this applies to in-app and email at once.
Bulk actions: mute, restore alerts, or unfollow several entities at once.
steps: Follow at least one entity.
Open Follow feed in the Account Center.
Filter by entity type or search by keyword.
Switch between new and upcoming releases, and mute entities when you want fewer alerts.
caveats: The feed relies on scheduled source checks every 30 minutes; retry later if a check fails.
Muting only affects alerts, not the follow relationship.
Whether a new work is available depends on the source site.

notification-center.title: Notification center
notification-center.summary: The bell at the top right shows recent notifications; Dashboard → Notifications has the full inbox and settings.
features: The bell shows the unread count, loads recent notifications page by page, and can mark everything read.

New-release notifications open Follow Feed filtered to that author; community notifications with a post open the post; feedback updates open My Feedback; other notifications with a code open search; announcements open their details in the inbox.
The page has two tabs, Inbox and Notification settings, with no separate community notification entry.
The inbox supports unread-only, pagination, deleting single items, and clearing read items.
Site announcements are merged with personal notifications rather than copied into the inbox.
Feedback replies and status changes create in-app notifications; the email reply is still sent separately when an admin opts in.
steps: Click the bell at the top right to see recent notifications.
Click a notification to jump to its target.
Open Dashboard → Notifications for the full list.
Filter or delete in the inbox, and adjust channels in notification settings.
caveats: Different notifications lead to different places; varying destinations are expected.
In-app and email switches are independent.
Announcement notifications usually cannot be turned off.

email-verification.title: Email verification
email-verification.summary: Verify your email before enabling email notifications. The code has 6 digits.
features: Send a 6-digit code to the current email from notification settings.
Codes expire in 15 minutes; you can resend after 60 seconds; after 5 wrong attempts, request a new code.
After verification, the email status becomes “Verified” and email switches become available.
The code has a countdown; you can resend after it ends.
steps: Go to Dashboard → Notifications → Notification settings.
Click “Verify email” on the email card.
Enter the 6-digit code you received and submit.
After verification, enable the email notifications you need.
caveats: All email switches are unavailable until the email is verified.
If the code does not arrive, check spam and confirm the email address.
Codes expire; request a new one after expiry.

email-preferences.title: Email preferences and privacy
email-preferences.summary: Each notification type controls in-app and email channels separately, and you can hide sensitive details from emails.
features: Types: new releases for follows, likes / comments / favorites on your posts, report results, and site announcements.
Channel switches: every type has an in-app and an email switch that work independently.
Hide email details: emails show only counts, without actress names or codes, and keep a neutral subject.
Digest sending: new activity is merged every 30 minutes, up to 3 emails per day, with the rest deferred.
Test email: after verification you can send one to confirm delivery.
steps: Go to Dashboard → Notifications → Notification settings.
Verify your email first.
Turn in-app and email on or off per type.
Enable “Hide email details” or send a test email as needed.
caveats: If email does not arrive, check spam, the verification status, and the matching switch.
Hiding details affects only the email body, not in-app notifications.
Digest sending delays some alerts; this is expected.

unsubscribe.title: Unsubscribing from email
unsubscribe.summary: Every notification email has a one-click unsubscribe link, and you can also turn email off in notification settings.
features: From email: click “Unsubscribe from email notifications” at the bottom and confirm.
Email only: in-app notifications are unaffected.
Resubscribe: turn the email switch for that type back on in notification settings.
Expired links: if the link no longer works, sign in and disable email notifications in the Account Center.
steps: Open any notification email.
Click the unsubscribe link at the bottom and confirm.
To restore, sign in and re-enable it in notification settings.
caveats: Unsubscribing does not cancel follows.
Some account emails, such as verification codes, are not affected.
Unsubscribe links can expire.

personal-center.title: Account Center
personal-center.summary: The Account Center gathers the overview, statistics, follow feed, my follows, favorites, history, notifications, activity, and sources; use the sidebar on desktop and the menu page on mobile.
features: Overview: welcome text, user level, and four metrics (searches, favorites, weekly sign-ins, sources) plus recent activity.
Library: follow feed, my follows, favorites, and history, with the same data as the home entries.
Messages: the notification inbox and my activity, which records sign-ins, searches, favorites, and settings changes.
Resources: sources, for maintaining personal sources and enabling system sources.
Account: profile and settings, plus the admin panel entry for admins.
steps: On desktop open the Dashboard group in the left sidebar; on mobile use the Dashboard bottom tab.
Start with the four overview metrics and recent activity.
Open favorites, history, or my follows to manage data.
On mobile the menu page appears first; click a feature to open its content page.
caveats: Everything in the Account Center is tied to the account and requires signing in.
My activity records account operations only, not browsing.
Overview metrics accumulate per account; switching accounts shows different numbers.

dashboard-stats.title: Statistics
dashboard-stats.summary: Statistics turns your search behavior into trends, a heatmap, and rankings so you can review your own habits.
features: Metric cards: total searches, weekly searches, unique keywords, total favorites, active days, and daily average.
A 30-day search trend and a weekly activity heatmap; hover for daily counts.
Top keywords, source usage distribution, and the top 10 search frequency ranking.
Shows your user level and how many actions remain to the next level.
steps: Open Dashboard → Statistics.
Use the trend and heatmap to spot peak times.
Use keyword and source distribution to see which sources you use most.
If it is empty, run a few searches and come back.
caveats: Statistics only cover the current account's history; clearing history also clears the source data.
Rankings show at most 10 entries.
Data is aggregated by day, so today's numbers may lag.

settings.title: Settings and appearance
settings.summary: Settings has three tabs: Profile, Security, and Appearance. Changes take effect immediately.
features: Profile: view and change the username (3–20 characters); “Change” next to the email swaps the address.
Security: change the password (6–100 characters) and use the danger zone to delete the account.
Appearance: theme (light, dark, or system) and language (简体中文, 繁體中文, English).
Theme and language share the same settings as the top-bar entries, so both stay in sync.
steps: Open settings from the avatar menu or the mobile Me page.
Change the username in Profile, or click “Change” next to the email (requires the current password and a code sent to the new address).
Change the password under Security; you must sign in again afterwards.
Pick a theme and language under Appearance.
caveats: Usernames and emails are checked for availability and format first; conflicts are reported on the matching field.
Changing the password invalidates the current session.
Deleting the account cannot be undone; back up favorites you want to keep.

register-login.title: Sign-up and sign-in
register-login.summary: Sign up with email, sign in with a password, or use GitHub / Google.
features: Sign-up: username 3–20 characters, password 6–100 characters, email verified with a 6-digit code.
Sign-in: use a username or email plus password; reset the password from the sign-in page if needed.
Registration switch: the site may close registration; the page then explains it, and existing accounts can still sign in.
Sign-out: the avatar menu or the mobile Me page.
steps: Open the sign-up page and fill in username, email, and password.
Enter the email code to finish registration.
Sign in with the username or email.
Use the avatar menu to sign out.
caveats: Passwords must be 6–100 characters.
Registration requires agreeing to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, both linked from the sign-up page and the landing-page footer.
A taken username or email is reported before the code is sent, so no email quota is wasted.
Do not share your account.

oauth.title: Third-party sign-in (OAuth)
oauth.summary: Sign in with GitHub or Google without a separate password.
features: Entry points: the GitHub / Google buttons below the sign-in form.
First sign-in creates or links an account and returns you to the site.
Callback failures: go back to the sign-in page and retry, or use a password instead.
steps: Click GitHub or Google on the sign-in page.
Authorize on the third-party page.
Wait to be returned to Atlas.
The first sign-in creates or links the account.
caveats: OAuth availability depends on whether the site has configured the app; a missing button means it is off.
Third-party account security is up to that platform.
On callback failures, avoid rapid repeated clicks and retry later.

email-password.title: Changing email and password
email-password.summary: Changing the email requires the current password and a code sent to the new address; changing the password requires signing in again.
features: Change email: Dashboard → Settings → Profile → “Change” next to the email.
The new address needs a 6-digit code and the current password.
Change password: Dashboard → Settings → Security → Change password.
You are signed out afterwards and must use the new credentials.
steps: Open Profile in the Account Center settings.
Click “Change” next to the email and enter the new address and current password.
Enter the code sent to the new address to finish.
For a password change, enter the current and new passwords.
caveats: Sign in with the new email afterwards.
Changing the password invalidates the current session.
New passwords must be 6–100 characters.

reset-password.title: Resetting a password
reset-password.summary: Reset the password with an email code, no old password needed.
features: Click “Forgot password” on the sign-in page.
Enter the registration email to get a 6-digit code.
Enter the code and a new password, then sign in.
steps: Click “Forgot password” on the sign-in page.
Enter the registration email and request a code.
Enter the code and the new password.
Sign in with the new password.
caveats: Codes expire and must be requested again.
Check spam if the email does not arrive.
Resetting the password does not lift account bans or limits.

delete-account.title: Deleting your account
delete-account.summary: Deletion permanently removes account data and cannot be undone.
features: Where: Dashboard → Settings → Security → Danger zone → Delete account.
You must read the impact, type the confirmation text, and enter an email code.
Profile, favorites, search history, custom sources, and other account data are removed.
steps: Open Dashboard → Settings → Security.
Find the danger zone and click Delete account.
Read the impact and confirm.
Enter the confirmation text and email code, then submit.
caveats: The account cannot be recovered after deletion.
If you only need a break, sign out instead.
Back up favorites you want to keep beforehand.

general-notices.title: General notices
general-notices.summary: Before using Atlas, understand the basics of content sources, account safety, email delivery, and data retention.
features: Sources and disclaimer: results, rankings, recommendations, online playback, and details come from third-party sites; Atlas only aggregates and indexes them.
Account safety: use a unique password, never share the account, and use codes only for your own actions.
Notifications and email: in-app notifications arrive immediately; email may be delayed by spam filters, blocking rules, or the provider.
Data retention: history, favorites, follows, and notifications live in your account, and deletion removes them.
Feedback: the button at the bottom right submits bugs and suggestions, and admin replies go to the contact email.
steps: Confirm the laws and personal-use boundaries that apply where you live.
Set a unique password and keep the email account secure.
Review notification settings and email verification periodically.
Delete data or the account from the Account Center when you need to.
caveats: Follow local laws and use the site only for lawful personal information lookup.
Third-party sites are responsible for their availability, content, and safety; judge the risk before opening links.
Never enter passwords, codes, or payment details into any third-party source page.
If email never arrives, check spam and blocking rules, then confirm the address is verified and the matching switch is on.
Features and wording may change; what the page shows is authoritative.

usage-limits.title: Usage limits and quotas
usage-limits.summary: Search, favorites, community writes, and registration are rate-limited to prevent abuse and protect data quotas. Admin accounts are exempt.
features: Search quotas are tiered and enforced per minute, hour, and day: Basic 5 / 40 / 200, Active 6 / 60 / 300, Regular 7 / 100 / 500, Core 8 / 160 / 800.

Tiers upgrade automatically and never downgrade: a 7-day-old account with 5 active days in the last 30 days becomes Active; 30 days plus 5 active days becomes Regular; 90 days, 5 active days, and 500 total searches becomes Core.
The current tier and this-minute usage are always shown next to the search box; click the question mark to see window usage and upgrade rules.
Other read endpoints: suggestions 30/min, trending keywords 20/min, tag recommendations 30/min, tag works 20/min.
Writes: favorites 5/min; posts 6/min, 30/hour, 100/day; comments 10/min, 60/hour, 300/day; post likes and favorites 30/min, 1000/day; reports 6/min, 30/day; custom tags 5/min, 50/day.
Registration is limited per IP to 5/min, 10/hour, 20/day; test emails are limited to 1/min per user.
Account data caps: up to 1,000 favorites and 1,000 history entries; follow up to 100 entities.
steps: Click the quota question mark next to the search box to see remaining search quota.
When quota runs out, wait for the matching window to reset (minute, hour, or next day) instead of retrying repeatedly.
On “too many requests” or 429, wait the number of seconds shown and try again.
To raise search quota, stay active and accumulate searches; tiers usually refresh within 24 hours.
caveats: Signed-out searches count per IP on the Basic tier; suggestions and trending also count per IP.
Tabs in the same account share quota, and the minute window guards against bursts.
Values may change with deployment configuration; the quota popover and actual prompts are authoritative.

faq-search.title: No results or very few results
faq-search.summary: Work through these steps in order; they usually pinpoint the cause quickly.
caveats: Change mode: if a JAV code returns nothing, try title or actress mode.
Change category: make sure the current category matches the content you want.
Check sources: run a health check on the Sources page or Dashboard → Sources, and confirm the source is online and enabled.
Check personal sources: a source you created must sit under the target major category or category and use a correct URL template.
Wait for quota: when quota runs out, wait as prompted instead of searching repeatedly.
Change keywords: try a shorter term, an alias, or drop extra symbols.

faq-access.title: Sources will not open or fail to load
faq-access.summary: When a source will not open, images are missing, or details fail to load, try these.
caveats: Turn on the proxy: for restricted sources, try the top-bar proxy first.
Try another source: an item often has several sources.
Retry: use retry when details fail; if it still fails, go back and search again.
Missing images: this is usually hotlink protection or network trouble; refresh or turn on the proxy. Covers use the site cache, so the second load is usually faster.
Playback will not open: try another platform or use the magnet link directly.
Proxy confirmation: the first time you enable the proxy a dialog explains it, and it only takes effect after you confirm.

faq-account.title: Account, code, and notification issues
faq-account.summary: How to troubleshoot sign-in problems, missing codes, and notifications that never appear.
caveats: No code: check spam, confirm the address, and resend after the countdown.
Username taken: the sign-up form reports it before sending a code; pick another name or sign in to the existing account.
OAuth username collision: the system appends a suffix and retries; if it still fails, register with email.
Signed out unexpectedly: sign in again; after changing the password or email, use the new credentials.
No email notifications: confirm the address is verified, the matching email switch is on, and you have not unsubscribed.
No in-app notifications: confirm the matching in-app switch is on and check the notification center for unread items.

faq-feedback.title: Sending feedback
faq-feedback.summary: In-site feedback is for bugs and suggestions; clear reproduction steps shorten handling time noticeably.
features: Entry: the feedback button at the bottom right of the landing and search pages.
Type: bug, suggestion, or other; title and content are required.
Contact email: defaults to the account email, and admin replies go there.
Feedback sent while signed in is linked to the account and appears in Dashboard → My Feedback.
Pending or closed feedback can be deleted in My Feedback; processing and resolved items keep their handling record.
steps: Click the feedback button at the bottom right.
Choose a type and describe the title and reproduction steps.
Confirm the contact email if you want a reply.
Track progress in My Feedback after submitting; replies or status changes trigger an in-app notification, and an email is sent when the admin opts in.
caveats: Never include passwords, verification codes, or payment information.
Replies are not guaranteed for every item; duplicates are merged.
For account-data issues, include roughly when it happened and which category you used.
Processing or resolved feedback cannot be deleted; deleting feedback is permanent.
